<thought>Based on the mass spectrum, the molecular ion appears at m/z 194.086 ([M+H]⁺), indicating a neutral mass of ~193.079 Da. The isotopic pattern (M+2 ≈ 33 % of M) suggests the presence of a single chlorine atom. A plausible molecular formula that fits this mass and includes one chlorine is C₈H₁₆NO₂Cl (exact monoisotopic mass 193.087 Da). This formula corresponds to a saturated chloro‑alkyl carbamate, for example the structure CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂OC(=O)NCH₃ with a chlorine on the terminal carbon. The SMILES for this candidate is **CCCCOC(=O)N(C)Cl**. This SMILES is valid and matches the inferred formula and chlorine presence. 

<final_answer>CCCCOC(=O)N(C)Cl</final_answer>
